units.summary: Lines 1-450 of app/domain/scenario/plan.py build the asset/systems text for the AI (cut to a budget), build the gate and gap-fill prompts, and validate and read the AI's per-threat verdicts and gap-fill proposals. A small dataclass (_ThreatFindingCalls) holds the run's models, pool and stop flag and runs gate batches in parallel with three recovery rules: halve a truncated batch once, re-ask badly answered slots once, and turn an unreadable first reply into a job retry. The rest pre-filters library threats by asset type/linked actor and turns verdicts into kept threats or recorded drops. The code is already fairly tight: class A savings here are small (about 30 lines); the larger cuts are class C recovery rules.

features.name: Asset and systems text for the AI (landscape)
features.what: Asset facts with leading keys first, organisation facts, each system by alias and quoted name; redacted; written, measured, facts cut to budget, rewritten, then hard-shortened; records is_cut for the trace

features.name: Gate / gap-fill prompt builder
features.what: System text + LANDSCAPE + STRIDE definitions + rules + labelled JSON items; prompt texts loaded from prompts.toml

features.name: Gate answer validation
features.what: Per slot: threat name copied, relevant bool, systems/entry_points aliases, categories with impact+reason, confidence 0-100, likelihood, reason when not relevant, needs list; problems feed the re-ask

features.name: Gate answer to Verdict
features.what: Builds Verdict: refusal (needs unrecorded / not relevant), attacker pick matched to listed names, actions, system ids, aliases replaced by system names, text caps

features.name: Gap-fill proposal validation
features.what: Reads {proposals:[...]} per asked category: applies bool, Pydantic contract, required threat_type/threat/reason, length cap, systems aliases

features.name: Gate batching in a shared pool
features.what: Slots R1..Rn, even batch size from THREATS_PER_QUESTION, further halving to fit the call token limit, batches run in a shared thread pool, verdicts returned in question order

features.name: Gate recovery rules
features.what: Stop flag after an outage; truncated batch halved once; badly answered slots re-asked once with their problems; unreadable first reply retries the job unless last attempt; else logged as not judged

features.name: Library pre-filter
features.what: Drops library threats whose asset type fits no place or that have no linked actor; silently skips custom-category-only threats

features.name: Library threats through the gate + entry-point check
features.what: Builds PlannedThreat candidates, asks the gate, then drops accepted threats whose entry points do not fit their asset type

features.name: Verdict to kept threat / drops
features.what: All-unanswered gate raises Unavailable; per candidate keeps named own categories, records a drop per lost category, copies verdict fields into the threat

units.summary: Lines 450-899 of plan.py finish threat finding and build the frozen plan. They turn gate verdicts into planned threats, ask the AI for a threat in each STRIDE category left empty and match it to a library type, merge duplicate and reworded threats, and fix each threat's main category and acting attacker. find_threats orchestrates this. build_plan ranks one path per threat, deals paths in turns across systems and marks the top N selected. build_plan_trace produces the stored plan-trace counts, drops and per-system tallies. Nothing here is dead; class A savings are small (about 30 lines), the larger cuts are class B/C.

features.name: Gate verdict to planned threat
features.what: Keeps categories the AI named among the threat's own, records a drop per lost category, raises Unavailable when no gate question was judged, copies systems, impact, likelihood and attacker pick.

features.name: Gap fill for empty categories
features.what: Lists STRIDE categories with no kept threat, asks the AI for one threat each, pre-embeds the proposals, builds candidates and sends them through the gate again.

features.name: Match AI threat to library type
features.what: Search plus rerank: drops a proposal that repeats a library threat, has no library type above the similarity threshold, or whose type links no attacker.

features.name: Merge duplicate and reworded threats
features.what: Three passes: same key, AI threat with a library threat's exact name and type, then embedding cosine (0.98 AI, 0.80 library). A merge unions categories, systems and reasons unless the asset type does not fit.

features.name: Main category and acting attacker
features.what: Orders the other categories in STRIDE order, resolves the gate's attacker pick against linked actors, drops the threat when no listed attacker fits.

features.name: find_threats orchestration
features.what: Refuses an empty actor library, builds the landscape, runs pre-filter, gate, gap fill, merge and attacker steps in one thread pool, returns ThreatFindings with counts and the library stamp.

features.name: Plan build and ranking
features.what: One path record per threat with a hashed path_id, ranked by risk, impact, confidence, STRIDE order, library before AI; top TOTAL_SCENARIO_COUNT selected, the rest marked target_reached.

features.name: Spread paths across systems
features.what: Deals ranked paths in turns over the supporting systems then the asset, saving a system's only remaining path for its turn; sets entry_system.

features.name: Plan trace
features.what: Stored trace for GET plan-trace: drops in a fixed 'most telling first' order capped at 300 with redacted details, per-stage counts, and per-system turns and groups.

units.summary: Lines 1-520 of app/domain/scenario/write.py turn one planned attack path into a writer brief (pre-flight refusals, fact trimming, stripping off-path system names from reasons/actions, evidence cleaning and cited-entry pick), build the batched writer prompt (shared facts once, then one SLOT block per path), and run a set in at most two AI calls (first write, then one rewrite of failed slots) with per-slot answer reading and an action-coverage check. Most of it is real feature logic pinned by goldens (tests/goldens/scenario/write_*.json store the full user prompt in "asks"). Invisible (class A) savings are small, about 40 lines: a one-use dataclass, a partial/parameter pair, can't-happen guards, duplicated brief fields, a 2-member enum. The large blocks (name stripping ~75 lines, shared-fact factoring ~14) are class C because they change the prompt text sent to the AI. No dead imports or unused constants were found in the scope.

features.name: Module constants and regexes

features.what: build_writer_input: gathers asset, systems, path facts, supporting systems, evidence into a WriterBrief plus casefolded brief_text for later id checks

features.what: 8 PathNotWritable checks: one threat, STRIDE category, named threat, acting attacker, none-fits, threat/attacker retired from live library, systems in run

features.what: Renames asset fact keys, adds country and organisation brief, redacts, cuts all text facts to one common length within budget (cut_to_fit)

features.name: Path BRIEF fields
features.what: category, attacker, why_this_attacker, likelihood word, threat type/name/actions/why, entry point options, supporting systems yes/no

features.what: Replaces names of systems not on the path in gate reasons with 'another system', repairing 'A, B and C' lists and 'the X'

features.name: Set writing in two AI calls

features.name: AI call batching and truncation handling
features.what: Halves a set until each call fits the token limit; a cut-off part is logged and skipped unless every part was cut

features.name: Answer reading per slot
features.what: Slot matching, & unescape, threat-name copy check, non-English check, pydantic contract, entry point settle, per-system reason fallback

features.name: Action coverage check

The code is already dense; real class-A slack is small (about 30 lines): a one-dependency class, a one-use rule dataclass, an app-dead helper and constant parameters. units.summary: Lines 1-420 of app/domain/scenario/session.py hold pure rules, no IO. First, the start check: it validates the request against the tsg_GetAssetContext rows (asset owned, systems linked, service/sector found), turns each row into JSON-safe facts, enforces required facts and freezes a FrozenContext. Second, plan progress: which attack paths to write next, plan counts, why nothing is left, and picking a spare path for a failed one. Third, review rules: session ownership, ready-for-review 409s, which scenarios can be accepted/rejected/regenerated, accept-all, replace-accepted and race results. The code is already flat functions with few one-use helpers; the real savings are feature cuts (class C), class A is small.

units.summary: app/domain/scenario/runs.py (561 lines) is the scenario module's use-case layer: start a run (idempotent replay, intel-data gate), read status/board/plan trace, page scenarios with their accepted/replaced versions, accept/reject, queue next-set and regenerate write jobs, and promote an AI threat to the library. All of it sits in one class, ThreatScenarioService, whose 11 constructor-injected collaborators are wired by a @singleton factory; nothing in app/ ever builds it differently. The sibling module app/domain/remediation/plans.py already does the same job as plain functions calling get_*_repository() directly, so the class and factory are pure plumbing (about 50 lines). Beyond that the file is fairly tight: remaining class A items are small pass-throughs and one-use helpers; the bigger cuts (race re-read, intel gate, controls resume) are user-visible and class C. Converting to functions needs test rework: 10 test files swap the service through dependency_overrides[get_threat_scenario_service] and tests/service_builders.py builds it with fakes.

units.summary: work_control.py is one class (WorkControlRepository, 4 injected repositories, singleton getter) holding the owner's job controls: list work in progress, cancel a run or plan, resume cancelled controls, delete a run, and the beat sweep that settles cancelled/deleted runs and re-queues stalled control mappings. tasks.py holds the four Celery tasks (find threats, write scenarios, map controls, retry controls) plus plan_run, which builds the plan and hands the first set to the write job. plan_progress.py is PlanProgress, the write job's fenced plan writes: abandon/replace a path, leave it for the next set, record states, continue or finish a set, finish a regenerate, and compute the two timings. Most of the 528 lines are real race guards and status bookkeeping; the removable weight is dependency plumbing (class + getter, partial/Callable injection, pass-through chains), about 60-70 lines class A. Bigger cuts here are all class C (race and orphan safeguards).

features.name: List work in progress
features.what: Queued/running runs (plus finished runs with controls still matching), plans and service mappings of an entity, oldest first, capped at LIST_MAX with a true total

features.name: Cancel a run
features.what: Stops the run's job, ends its next-set/regenerate summary as cancelled at the same epoch, cancels its waiting controls, stamps a finished run whose controls were stopped

features.name: Cancel a remediation plan
features.what: Stops the plan's job, cancels a manual scenario's controls, hands a generated scenario's held controls back to the run (queued or cancelled), recounts

features.name: Resume cancelled controls
features.what: Re-queues controls a cancel stopped; undone if a newer cancel or a delete races it; optionally restarts the run's timings

features.name: Delete a run
features.what: Marks the run deleting, refuses while any job/controls/plan works, deletes SQL operation records, scenarios, plans, then the run

features.name: Controls sweep
features.what: Beat: cancel controls waiting on a cancelled run, delete scenarios of a deleted run, fail abandoned and re-queue stalled controls, return runs needing a message

features.name: Find-threats task and plan_run
features.what: Leased job: find threats, build plan and trace, stamp made_with, set counts and threats time, hand first set to the write task or end the run done

features.name: Write-scenarios task
features.what: Leased job wrapper that calls the write job

features.name: Map-controls task with outage retries
features.what: Runs controls mapping; on a temporary error shows an outage notice with retry time and retries with backoff up to MAX_MESSAGE_RETRIES, then leaves it to the sweep

features.name: Abandon and replace a path
features.what: Gives a path up for good, counts the metric, swaps in a reserve path and adds it to the set being written

features.name: Leave a path for the next set / settled-by-this-job
features.what: Keeps a path open but out of this set; a path settled at this epoch is not written again by a redelivery

features.name: Fenced plan record
features.what: Saves path states, plan figures and scenario counts in one fenced write, counts metrics, publishes status

features.name: Continue or finish a set
features.what: Hands the next batch to the same task or ends the set: rescues given-up paths that do have a scenario, sets complete/partial, next-set summary, timings

features.name: Finish regenerate and action timings
features.what: Ends a regenerate complete/partial with replaced count; splits the latest action's time into threats_s and scenarios_s

units.summary: write_job.py runs one Celery delivery of a scenario batch: load the run, pick open paths, skip repeats, attach evidence (if intelligence is on), write the set, save cards, queue control mapping, settle outages, move the run on. path_writing.py builds each path's brief and turns AI faults into per-path outcomes (PathWriter), then saves cards or regenerated versions with unique titles and updates plan state (PathSaver). Real logic is about 330 of 466 lines; the rest is wiring: a singleton+partial job factory, three classes built once each that pass run/lease/repos/threats to each other, a type alias, and one-use helpers. Nothing is dead outright, but one flag is write-only and several guards cover states the planner cannot produce.

features.name: Batch orchestration
features.what: Order of one delivery: pick paths, drop repeats, evidence, stamp writing_started_at, write, queue controls, settle outages, continue or finish (regenerate vs set).

features.name: Job wiring
features.what: write_scenario_batch + get_scenario_write_job singleton/partial + BatchWriter ctor + EvidenceParts alias: loads run, library, switch, repos and builds 4 collaborators.

features.name: Evidence outage hold-back
features.what: A path whose threat's evidence search failed or never ran is not written; it waits with the search's own outage message.

features.name: Pre-write repeat check
features.what: Before any AI call a first-write path that repeats a held scenario of the run is abandoned as NEAR_DUPLICATE, its failure card updated, a spare may replace it.

features.name: Outage settling
features.what: On the last lease attempt, if every error is Unavailable and something was served (or regenerate), paths get failure cards with outage text; else the most retryable error is raised.

features.name: Set writing and control queueing
features.what: Labels slots SC1.., streams outcomes, saves each as final, sends MAP_CONTROLS per served path and once more after the set.

features.name: Brief building and fault mapping
features.what: PathWriter: builds briefs, maps PathNotWritable, unreadable/truncated answers, temporary errors and unexpected faults to per-path failures or errors.

features.name: Unique title save
features.what: Saves under title, then title (threat), then title (2), (3).. until the unique index accepts it.

features.name: Open-path selection and crash healing
features.what: to_write/_versions_to_write: paths still open; ones already written by a crashed delivery are served without an AI call; half-done regenerate supersedes are healed.

features.name: Save outcome and path state
features.what: Failure card or written card saved with generation stamp; then served / left for next set (Unavailable under max attempts) / abandoned with reason and metric.

features.name: Regenerate version save
features.what: New version saved then old superseded; a failed or blocked rewrite only notes regenerate_error on the old version.

features.name: Post-write duplicate check and held list
features.what: A written scenario matching a held one gets a NEAR_DUPLICATE finding (blocked); the run's held list is read lazily once and kept current in memory.

features.name: Save logging and metric
features.what: _log_saved logs every save and counts WRITTEN.

units.summary: controls_job.py (281 lines) is the tsg_map_controls worker: one delivery takes a per-run delivery lease, claims up to 6 written scenarios, embeds their control queries in one call, maps each under its own renewed lease, saves the mapping, recounts and publishes. Real logic is about 90 lines (claim, map, outcome handling, turn hand-over); the other ~150 are wiring: a 7-arg class constructor, a singleton+partial getter, a Future/Lock one-shot class, a lease class. Sweep (15 lines here, beat every 300 s) recovers lost messages, crashed workers and failed-with-attempts-left cards. Retry notice (13 lines) shows an outage on the run status. Give-back (10 lines) requeues at worker stop without burning an attempt.

features.name: Delivery entry and per-run delivery lease (turn taking)
features.what: Claim the run's controls_delivery lease, map up to PER_DELIVERY=6, then release (re-send if more wait) or hand over the next turn; stop if taken over. Caps one delivery per run; local reranker maps 1 at a time.

features.name: Stalled-controls sweep (beat)
features.what: Every 300 s: settle cancelled/deleted runs' cards, fail abandoned (5 attempts), requeue queued>600 s, expired running leases and failed>30 min; recount, publish, log, send one message per run with no live delivery.

features.name: Recount and publish
features.what: Recount a run's counts, add controls seconds to timings (latest action only), publish status to watchers.

features.what: Claim oldest waiting scenarios one by one (atomic find_one_and_update); read the run's frozen context once, only when something was claimed; deleted run yields nothing.

features.name: One embedding call per turn
features.what: Build each claimed scenario's control query and embed all in one call; done by the first mapping thread under its lease, others wait on a Future checking their own lease; an outage is replayed to every waiter.

features.name: Map one scenario and settle outcome
features.what: Map under a renewed lease; empty library or fault fails that scenario only; outage requeues it with the error and retries the message; lost lease is silent; DONE saved by fenced write.

features.name: Per-scenario log context and timing
features.what: Bind the writer's request id/origin to logs, time the mapping, recount+publish after each, renew delivery lease and detect take-over.

features.name: Scenario lease renew and give-back at worker stop
features.what: Renewer thread extends scenario and delivery leases; a stopping worker requeues the scenario without counting the attempt, frees the delivery lease and re-sends the message.

units.summary: app/schemas/scenario_internal.py (442 lines) holds 24 internal shapes for the scenario module: the stored-procedure rows, the frozen asset context, control query/rule/mapping, the gate verdict and planned threat, plan drops and findings, the writer brief/draft/findings, the path failure, and two AI-answer contracts. Only FrozenContext, PlannedThreat, Drop, WriterBrief, WrittenScenario and PathFailure are widely shared (11-52 app references each). About ten shapes have one producer and one consumer (ControlRule, MappedControl, ControlMapping, PlannedActor, AttackPlace, ActorPick, LiveLibrary, BriefSystem, AssetContextRows, GapFillResponse) and exist only to be turned into a dict or read once. FrozenContext still carries old-saved-format tolerance (from_record key filter, linked_systems fallback). Substantiated net saving is roughly 125 app lines, nearly all class A; test churn is noticeable because tests construct these classes directly (e.g. 65 from_record/linked_systems/to_record uses, 35 mapping.attr reads). Verdict, Landscape, ThreatFindings, ControlQuery, ScenarioDraft and Drop are multi-field, multi-reader and worth keeping.

units.summary: evidence.py finds each threat's evidence at write time: it embeds the threat's type+name, takes candidates from the in-memory ATT&CK index, reranks them (behind a per-process gate and a score cache), keeps those over the threshold (else the nearest), and stores evidence plus an audit of the search on the threat. Outages never fail a batch: the threat gets a failure record and its paths wait. switch.py is the on/off switch: env flag AND an admin flag in Mongo, cached 60 s per process with single-flight reads and outage fallbacks. Both files are small (432 lines) but carry constructor injection kept only for tests, a second rerank limiter on top of the AI slots, and a kind-diversity rule that is dead now that ATT&CK techniques are the only source.

features.name: Per-process rerank gate
features.what: Bounded semaphore (CII_RERANKS_AT_ONCE remote, 1 local) around each rerank; a waiter checks its job lease every 2 s

features.name: Batch evidence search
features.what: One embedding call for all requests, then reranks 8 at once; an embedding outage fails all requests softly, a rerank outage only its own request

features.name: Switch: env AND admin flag, cached

units.summary: app/domain/intel/index.py reads the approved sources' current records from MongoDB into a corpus with an order-independent checksum, embeds them into a hybrid (word + vector) index, and serves per-threat candidate search and reranker scoring with indicators (URLs, IPs, hashes) stripped. EvidenceIndexKeeper holds one index per process: background build on a thread with a Future, exponential retry after a failed build, a placeholder index that carries the AI outage, a 60 s check of the active-snapshot pointer so every process follows the newest build, and publishing of the snapshot description. Nearly all collaborators (3 repositories, 2 AI models, 2 model names, clock) are constructor-injected and threaded through 5 functions, though the app has exactly one wiring (get_evidence_index_keeper). Tests under tests/external_intelligence inject fakes through those parameters, so most plumbing cuts need test edits.

units.summary: The three files are the prompt-injection defence for external (ATT&CK) text. patterns.py is a data file of compiled regex tables (instruction phrases, live markup, squashed phrases, encoded blobs, look-alike letters, plus the writer's echo table). safety.py normalises untrusted text, strips markup in up to 4 rounds, checks several views (text, skeleton, squashed, plain) against the tables, tells hashes/paths from encoded payloads, and cuts at a sentence end. facts.py re-sanitises stored strings and builds the plain evidence sentences, title, link and mitigation names for a technique, with a name-grammar rule. Most of the bulk is the security control itself; the removable part is class/DI plumbing (4 classes that only hold a default-constructed sanitiser), a search memo, and a handful of one-use helpers. Realistic class-A saving is about 60 lines of 643; anything bigger is class C.

features.what: A long run is allowed when it is a path of short pieces or a digest-length hex that does not decode to printable text

units.summary: The intel-store unit holds the stored shapes (19 dataclasses/enums in schemas/intel_records.py), three Mongo repositories (feed status with refresh claims, records with versions, snapshot pointer), the admin service behind 7 frozen /v1/tsg/intel routes, the Celery refresh task with worker warm-up and a follow thread, and the API models plus cited-evidence view. With only ATT&CK left, several fields are constant: FetchResult.partial/more and more_pending are always False, Evidence.applicability always None, joined always empty, 4 of 5 IntelKind members and 4 of 5 corpus counters unused. The refresh builds a rich per-source result (5 outcomes, counts, retired, error) of which the app reads only the failed sources and index_error. Rejected records are written to tsg_intel as quarantined rows that no code reads. The admin class and worker functions carry dependency plumbing (10 constructor arguments, provider callables) that every caller fills the same way. Not verified: whether the three repository getters could become module-level instances (MongoRepository import-safety unread).

units.summary: Scenario code is wired three ways at once: a constructor-injected service class (ThreatScenarioService, 11 collaborators) behind a @singleton getter and FastAPI Depends; @singleton getters returning partial(...) for the write and controls jobs; and Callable parameters (plan_run, sweep recount). Models and repositories then travel 4-6 hops through BatchWriter/PathWriter/PathSaver/PlanProgress/RunControls/ControlMapper/_ScenarioLease constructors before the one call that uses them. app/domain/jobs.py already uses the direct style (module functions calling getters), so the pattern exists in-repo. units.summary: Read-only review of the scenario module's data shapes (14 files, 5,947 lines). One scenario passes through about 12 shapes: gate answer dict -> Verdict -> PlannedThreat (+AttackPlace, ActorPick, PlannedActor) -> plan threat/path dicts -> WriterBrief -> ScenarioAnswer -> ScenarioDraft -> WrittenScenario/Finding -> card dict -> ScenarioView; controls go LibraryControl -> MappedControl -> ControlMapping -> record dict -> ControlView. The stored dicts and the v1 API view are frozen, so the ~350-line view mapping stays; the savings are in the one-hop dataclasses between them (about 20 in scenario_internal.py, most built in exactly one place). The run status lists the same 19 fields three times (projection, model, copier). runs.py still has a service class with 11 injected collaborators, against ADR 004. Substantiated net saving is roughly 320 lines, nearly all class A; no API, prompt or stored-name change is needed except where flagged B/C.

units.summary: Scope: scenario run lifecycle (start, plan threats, write sets, regenerate, map controls, review, cancel/delete) plus the shared leased-job machinery. The same rules are written several times: mapping one claimed scenario (controls job and plan job), saving run counts, counting plan paths, marking a path served, validating review/regenerate targets, building error and retry records. Three jobs are wired three different ways (partial, singleton getter, nested closure), and 9 small classes mostly hold injected singletons. Controls carry three stacked retry mechanisms and two nested leases. About 290 lines are class A, about 55 class B, about 115 class C. Nothing was run; estimates come from reading only.

units.summary: The scenario module plans a run (library threats judged by an AI gate in batches, AI gap-fill for empty STRIDE categories, duplicate merge, one ranked path per threat), writes scenarios a set at a time (brief, one AI call plus a rewrite call, code checks, card save), then maps library controls per card in a separate background job. Runs, review (accept/reject/regenerate/next set/promote) and the status board sit in runs.py and session.py over two Mongo repositories. The file-by-file audit covered dependency plumbing and small rules well; what it missed is mostly duplication across files: controls mapping is a second leased-job system beside the generic one, the writer and paths have retry ladders stacked on the job's own, and several zones of write.py (lines 391-526, 962-1022), plan.py's merge stage (564-659) and domain/shared/names.py got no findings at all. Nothing was run or changed; all line numbers are from reading the current working tree.

flow.report:
END-TO-END FLOW (working tree, branch tsg_simplify_codebase_2026-11-16_16-25; read-only trace, nothing run)

A. Start run (HTTP)
1. POST /v1/sessions -> app/api/routes/scenarios.py:37 start_run; deps: Caller, IdempotencyKey (app/api/deps.py:55-85), Scenarios = Depends(get_threat_scenario_service) (runs.py:497 @singleton wiring 11 collaborators).
2. runs.py:94 ThreatScenarioService.create_threat_scenario_session (decorator origin_of_its_jobs, domain/shared/audit.py:19): _replay 121 (idempotency) -> _refuse_without_intel_data 114 -> AssetRepository.get_asset_context (crud/scenarios.py:636, SQL stored procedure) -> session.build_run_context (session.py:31-190) -> _new_run_record 521.
3. crud/scenarios.py:472 create_scenario_session (insert; RunClash on key clash) -> runs.py:138 _announce_start: send_job(FIND_THREATS) (worker/celery_app.py:136), metric, audit record -> session.build_status_board (session.py:448) -> 202 RunBoard.

B. Find threats (queue tsg_threats)
4. worker/scenario/tasks.py:28 find_threats -> worker/jobs.py:98 run_leased_job (claim 158, keep_lease_alive, retry/fail 178, publish) -> tasks.py:81 plan_run with partial(plan.find_threats, chat, search, rerank, embeddings).
5. domain/scenario/plan.py:686 find_threats: library snapshot -> describe_asset_for_ai 66 -> _list_threats_to_check 389 -> _find_library_threats_that_apply 405 (AI gate in batches, _ThreatFindingCalls 294-388, 24 h answer reuse) -> _add_ai_threats_for_empty_categories 498 -> _merge_duplicate_threats 564 (embeddings) -> _set_main_category_and_attacker 662.
6. plan.py:746 build_plan (rank, spread_paths_across_systems 806, select target) -> session.pick_next_paths_to_write (session.py:220) -> plan.py:826 build_plan_trace -> worker/jobs.py:61 hand_over: one fenced write of plan + job.batch/job.set, then send_job(WRITE_SCENARIOS).

C. Write scenarios (queue tsg_scenarios)
7. tasks.py:44 write_scenarios -> run_leased_job -> write_job.py:66 get_scenario_write_job (singleton partial) -> write_job.py:52 write_scenario_batch (reads run, library, intel switch) -> BatchWriter (74) builds PlanProgress, PathWriter, PathSaver, EvidenceAtWrite.
8. BatchWriter.write 103: PathSaver.to_write (path_writing.py:159) -> _drop_repeated_paths 143 -> EvidenceAtWrite.attach (domain/intel/evidence.py:277) + _is_held_back 166 -> _write_set 124.
9. path_writing.py:42 PathWriter.write_scenario_set: write.build_writer_input (write.py:91) per path -> write.py:367 write_scenario_set: _ask_writer 428 (1 AI call per set) -> _read_scenario_draft 461 -> _apply_safety_checks 564 -> _find_actions_missing_from_story 503 -> _rewrite_failed_scenarios 391 (1 more AI call).
10. path_writing.py:178 PathSaver.save: write.build_scenario_card 590 / build_failure_card 674 -> find_duplicate_scenario_id 754 -> save_with_unique_title 84 -> crud save_scenario (crud/scenarios.py:201) -> PlanProgress.record / leave_for_next_set / abandon (plan_progress.py:43-91; fenced write, counts, publish) -> send_job(MAP_CONTROLS) per served card (write_job.py:136).
11. write_job.py:174 _settle_outages (retry the job or write failure cards on the last attempt) -> PlanProgress.continue_or_finish (plan_progress.py:93: hand_over to the same task for the set's next batch, or end job DONE with timings).

D. Map controls (queue tsg_controls)
12. tasks.py:54 map_controls (own retry ladder 60-69) -> controls_job.py:42 map_threat_scenario_controls: claim_controls_delivery (crud/scenarios.py:585) -> RunControls.map_all 127: claim_scenario_controls (crud 271) -> _OneEmbedCall 221 -> _map_one 181 under _ScenarioLease 252 -> write.ControlMapper.map_controls (write.py:796: build_control_query 962, search+rerank 860, pick_controls_to_keep 918) -> update_scenario_controls (crud 313) -> recount_and_publish 91.
13. Beat: tasks.py:72 retry_controls -> controls_job.py:75 -> crud/work_control.py:233 sweep_stalled_controls; worker/jobs.py:230 reap_jobs re-queues expired/unsent jobs.

E. Later actions
14. Next set: routes 155 -> runs.py:368 -> pick_next_paths_to_write -> _queue_write_job 406 (crud update_scenario_session_job 499, send WRITE_SCENARIOS, audit) or _resume_controls 433; 409 nothing_left/target_reached/scenarios_abandoned.
15. Regenerate: routes 140 -> runs.py:395 -> session.build_regenerate_batch (session.py:400) -> _queue_write_job; worker: PathSaver._versions_to_write 208, _save_version 232, supersede_scenario_version 100, PlanProgress.finish_regenerate 124.
16. Accept/reject: routes 114/130 -> runs.py:249/272 (_chosen, _make_room, _decide, _announce_decisions). Promote: routes 167 -> runs.py:441.
17. Hand-written scenario: POST treatment-plan with is_manual=true (routes/remediation.py:29) -> domain/remediation/plans.py:176 _create_manual_plan -> _save_manual_scenario 242 -> crud create_manual_scenario_session (crud/scenarios.py:487); worker/remediation.py:116-139, 247-270.
18. Cancel: routes/jobs.py:20 -> domain/jobs.py:97 -> work_control.cancel_scenario_session 78. Delete: routes/jobs.py:27 -> domain/jobs.py:112 -> work_control.delete_scenario_session 175 (409 cancel_first).

F. Reads
19. Status: routes 58 -> valid_session (deps.py:111, one Mongo read) -> build_status_board (session.py:448-586). Results/one/entity lists: routes 66-100 -> runs.py:169-247 -> build_scenario_view (session.py:587-809). Plan trace: routes 103 -> runs.py:183 -> session.py:810.
20. Stream: routes 186 -> api/status_stream.py:15 (EventHub.listen, re-read on publish or every RECHECK_SECONDS, API-key re-check) <- realtime/publisher.py:15 publish_session_status called after every saved change.

COUNTS FOR ONE "GENERATE" CLICK
- Scenario-own files: 13 (6,159 lines): routes/scenarios.py 214, runs.py 560, session.py 835, plan.py 899, write.py 1022, tasks.py 114, write_job.py 193, path_writing.py 273, plan_progress.py 144, controls_job.py 281, crud/scenarios.py 668, schemas/scenarios.py 514, schemas/scenario_internal.py 442.
- Those 13 files hold 289 defs and 69 classes (54 are Pydantic/dataclass models). My estimate, not a measured trace: about 230 of the defs run for start + plan + write + controls + status; the rest are review, promote, regenerate, manual and remediation-only crud.
- Classes with behaviour on the path: 17 (ThreatScenarioService, 3 repositories, _ThreatFindingCalls, BatchWriter, PathWriter, PathSaver, PlanProgress, EvidenceAtWrite, EvidenceFinder, RunControls, _OneEmbedCall, _ScenarioLease, ControlMapper, JobLease, JobRepository).
- Shared files also entered: about 20 (api/deps.py, worker/jobs.py 354, crud/jobs.py 248, celery_app.py, lease_renewal.py, crud/work_control.py 270, domain/intel/evidence.py 334 and switch.py, domain/shared ask_ai/parallel/audit/idempotency, realtime publisher + event_hub, api/status_stream.py, search service/snapshot/library_cache, ai chat/rerank/embeddings, crud/base.py).
- Celery hops: 3 tasks (find -> write, re-sent per batch -> map controls, re-sent per delivery) + 2 beat tasks. AI chat calls: gate batches + gap fill in planning, at most 2 per written set.

WHAT A PLANNER SHOULD NOTICE (not cut proposals, just shape)
- The write job spreads one loop over 4 classes in 3 worker files (BatchWriter, PathWriter, PathSaver, PlanProgress) plus write.py; each holds the same lease/run/repositories passed through constructors.
- Dependency plumbing still present despite ADR-004: ThreatScenarioService + get_threat_scenario_service singleton (runs.py:71-518), get_scenario_write_job/get_controls_job partials, plan_run taking find_threats as a Callable.
- Two separate lease systems: the run's job lease (worker/jobs.py + crud/jobs.py) and the controls delivery lease + per-scenario lease (controls_job.py, crud/scenarios.py:585-628).
- Line counts in items are approximate (read from function ranges), and overlap between features.

items.name: Start a run (idempotent)
items.what: POST /v1/sessions returns 202 with a status board; a retry with the same Idempotency-Key returns the same run (200); the same body within a minute without a key is 409 duplicate_request.
items.where: routes/scenarios.py:37-55; runs.py:94-147, 521-545; api/deps.py:50-85; crud/scenarios.py:472-478; session.py:31-190 (asset facts and checks)

items.name: Asset context frozen at start
items.what: The asset, its supporting systems, service and sector are read once from SQL, checked (required facts, linked systems), and frozen on the run so later sets and regenerates use the same facts.

items.name: Refuse when intelligence has no data
items.what: 409 intel_no_data on start, next set and regenerate when external intelligence is switched on but nothing is imported yet.

items.name: Find the threats that apply
items.what: The library's threats that fit the asset type are put to the AI in batches (applies or not, which systems, which attacker); answers are reused for 24 h.

items.name: AI-proposed threats for empty categories
items.what: Where no library threat applies in a threat category, the AI proposes one; it is matched to a library type and attacker or dropped.

items.name: Merge near-copy threats, pick attacker
items.what: Reworded or duplicate threats are joined (embedding similarity) and each kept threat gets one main category and one listed attacker.

items.name: Ranked plan with a scenario target
items.what: One path per threat, ranked, dealt in turns across the supporting systems; the best N (total_scenario_count) are selected, the rest stay as spares.

items.name: Plan trace
items.what: GET /v1/sessions/{id}/plan-trace: how many candidates each planning stage took in and let out, every drop with reason, and what became of the planned paths.

items.name: Write scenarios in sets
items.what: The first set (initial_set_size) is written in one AI call per set; each scenario is saved and shown as soon as it is final; a draft with problems gets one rewrite call.
items.where: write.py:91-560 (brief, prompts, _ask_writer, draft reading, rewrite); path_writing.py:32-82; write_job.py:52-137

items.name: Safety checks on written text
items.what: A scenario citing an id it was not given, an unknown citation marker, or echoing injected evidence text gets a finding; blocking findings keep the card from being served.
items.protects_against: AI text that invents ids or repeats prompt-injection text from untrusted evidence reaching the user.

items.name: Evidence from external intelligence
items.what: With intelligence on, each threat's evidence is searched before writing and the scenario carries an evidence sentence and link; a failed search holds the path back instead of writing it uncited.

items.name: No repeated scenario in a run
items.what: A path whose threat/system repeats an already written scenario of the run is abandoned (near_duplicate) and titles are made unique within the run.
items.where: write.py:754-789; write_job.py:143-164; path_writing.py:84-97, 127-134, 245-273; crud TitleTaken index

items.name: Failure cards and per-path retries
items.what: A path the AI could not write shows as a failure card with its reason; an outage leaves it for a later set (up to MAX_PATH_ATTEMPTS) and then abandons it.

items.name: Spare path replaces a failed one
items.what: When a selected path is given up, the best unselected path is selected in its place within the same set, so the user still gets the target number of scenarios.

items.name: Map controls to each scenario
items.what: Each written scenario gets library controls (embedding search + reranker, min/max/threshold rules) in the background; status shows controls waiting, mapped or failed.

items.name: Controls sweep (beat task)
items.what: Every minute stalled or abandoned control mappings are re-queued or failed and one message is re-sent per run that no delivery holds.
items.protects_against: Control mappings stuck in running for ever after a worker crash or lost broker message.

items.name: Write the next set
items.what: POST .../scenarios/next-set writes the next NEXT_SET_SIZE open paths; 409 nothing_left, target_reached or scenarios_abandoned; on a cancelled run it resumes the controls.

items.name: Regenerate scenarios with versions
items.what: POST .../regenerate/scenarios writes a new version of each chosen scenario; the old version stays readable under the new one; a failed rewrite is noted on the old version.

items.name: Accept and reject scenarios
items.what: Accept a subset, all or none (v1 and v2 bodies), optionally replacing an accepted older version; reject a list; each skipped id comes back with its reason.

items.name: Promote an AI threat to the library
items.what: An accepted scenario whose threat the AI proposed is sent to the curators as a pending library threat; set once, repeat is quiet.

items.name: Run status board
items.what: GET /v1/sessions/{id}: overall state, per-stage state (threats, scenarios, controls), counts, timings of the latest action, errors and retry notices.

items.name: Read scenarios (run, one, entity)
items.what: Paged results of a run with replaced versions, one scenario in full, and every current scenario of the entity filtered by decision.

items.name: Live status stream (SSE)
items.what: GET .../events sends session.updated at every saved change and session.deleted once; re-reads on a timer if a publish was missed and ends when the API key is revoked.
items.where: routes/scenarios.py:180-198; api/status_stream.py:1-51; realtime/event_hub.py:1-100; realtime/publisher.py:1-42 (shared with plans and mapper)

items.name: Cancel and delete a run
items.what: Cancel stops the run's job and its control mappings (409 nothing_to_cancel); delete removes the run, scenarios and plans for good (409 cancel_first while anything works).

items.name: Hand-written scenario
items.what: A person's own scenario sent with a plan request (is_manual=true) is saved as a manual run and scenario, resolved to a library threat and controls, and accepted at once.

items.name: Job lease, retries and reaper
items.what: Each job runs under a renewed lease with an epoch fence; outages retry up to MAX_ATTEMPTS with a retry notice on the status; the reaper re-queues expired or unsent jobs.
items.where: worker/jobs.py:1-354; crud/jobs.py:1-248; worker/lease_renewal.py; shared by scenario, remediation and mapper
items.protects_against: A crashed worker, lost broker message or duplicate delivery leaving a run stuck or written twice.

items.name: Audit records and metrics
items.what: Start, next set, regenerate, accept, reject, promote, cancel and delete each write an audit record and bump a metric; timings per stage are stored on the run.

mechanisms.report:
Read-only inventory of 26 runtime mechanisms (no files changed, nothing run). Line counts are approximate, counted from the files read.

SHARED BY ALL THREE MODULES (scenario, remediation, service mapper) - about 1,620 lines; removing any is not a scenario-only decision:
- Job lease, claim and fence; lease renewal thread; lease-lost signal; epoch; reaper (expired leases, lost-message re-send, job gauges); outage back-off with MAX_ATTEMPTS; job.retry notice; shutdown hand-back; message priority; send_job; worker lifecycle (heartbeat, job clock).
- Status publish (Redis pub/sub) and the SSE stream: 3 publishers, 3 stream routes.
- Idempotency key dependency (scenario start, remediation plan, mapper create and regenerate).
- Same-job AI answer reuse (4 callers: plan.py:375, scenario write.py:438, remediation/write.py:429, service_mapper/generate.py:45).
- Jobs list and admin monitor (app/domain/jobs.py).
Files: app/worker/jobs.py 354, app/crud/jobs.py 248, app/worker/lease_renewal.py 76, app/core/lease_signal.py 58, app/realtime 142, app/api/status_stream.py 51, app/worker/lifecycle.py 227, app/worker/celery_app.py 153, app/domain/jobs.py 308.

SHARED INFRASTRUCTURE WITH NO SCENARIO USER:
- Waiting-for-another-job (about 30 lines in worker/jobs.py): raised only at app/worker/remediation.py:177, 199, 205.
- BUSY_ENTITY_PRIORITY: used only at app/domain/remediation/plans.py:313.

SCENARIO-ONLY - about 1,000 lines in app/worker/scenario plus about 350 in app/crud/work_control.py and app/crud/scenarios.py:
- The controls stage runs a second, parallel lease system because tsg_map_controls does not use run_leased_job: a per-run delivery lease (about 70 lines), a per-scenario controls lease (about 110), its own sweep on a 300 s beat (about 100), its own message retry ladder and its own retry notice (about 20). It repeats lease, reaper, back-off and notice once more. send_job passes epoch 0 with the comment "the epoch is never checked for controls" at 5 sites. This is the largest scenario-only runtime cost. Folding controls into the leased job would be class B, but the per-scenario controls.* fields and the controls_delivery field are stored names, and remediation's plan job claims the same scenario lease (app/worker/remediation.py:169-217).
- Plan progress and counts (about 200 lines), crash-safe re-delivery of the write job (about 55), per-stage timings (about 45), scenario outage settling (about 75), hand_over to the next stage (2 callers), cancel/resume/delete of a run (about 190), cross-run threat-finding reuse (about 10, switchable off with CII_THREAT_FINDING_REUSE_HOURS=0).

USER-VISIBLE, SO CLASS C IF REMOVED: retry notices (`retrying`), `epoch` in RunActionStarted, stage timings, cancel/delete/jobs-list endpoints, 409 duplicate_request, SSE events, generation_epoch.

CLASS A PLUMBING SEEN IN THESE FILES:
- get_scenario_write_job and get_controls_job are singleton + partial(...) with one call site each (app/worker/scenario/tasks.py:49, :59).
- tasks.py:39 builds partial(plan.find_threats, *models) for one caller.
- BatchWriter, PlanProgress, PathSaver, RunControls and _ScenarioLease take repositories by constructor that are module-level getters anyway.
- WorkControlRepository (app/crud/work_control.py:48-59, 260-270) only holds 4 injected repositories.
- app/domain/jobs.py:198-225 and :304-308 are lazy-import wrappers.
- recount/Recount callback in the sweep has 1 caller (controls_job.py:84).
- JobLease.renew is an alias of renew_job (app/crud/jobs.py:120).

items.name: Job lease: claim and fence
items.what: claim_job atomically flips queued->running with task_id, attempts+1 and lease_until; JobLease.fence makes every later write match only while this delivery owns the record, else LeaseLost. run_leased_job wraps claim, work, fail.
items.where: SHARED (all 3). app/crud/jobs.py:24-120,139-171; app/worker/jobs.py:85-132,144-175. Callers: scenario/tasks.py:41,51; worker/remediation.py:294; worker/service_mapper.py:26
items.protects_against: Two deliveries of one message (Redis redelivery, reaper re-send) both running the job and both writing scenarios; a cancelled or superseded job overwriting newer state.

items.name: Lease renewal thread
items.what: keep_lease_alive starts a daemon thread per job that extends job.lease_until every 30 s (lease 120 s); a failed renew sets the lost signal. PlanProgress.hold also renews right before each scenario save.
items.where: SHARED. app/worker/lease_renewal.py:24-60; app/crud/jobs.py:112-120. Scenario extra: plan_progress.py:38-41, controls_job.py:187, remediation.py:186
items.protects_against: A long AI call (minutes) outliving a fixed lease, so the reaper requeues a healthy job and it runs twice; without renewal the lease would need to be an hour and a dead pod's job would sit that long.

items.name: Lease-lost signal
items.what: ContextVar stack of threading.Events set by the renewer; raise_if_lease_lost is checked before every AI slot wait/call, wait_while_leased polls it every 1 s while waiting on shared work.
items.where: SHARED. app/core/lease_signal.py (58). 10 check sites: ai/slots.py x6, ai/rerank.py:108, intel/evidence.py:60,62, lease_renewal.py:74; wait_while_leased: search/service.py:59, controls_job.py:239
items.protects_against: A cancelled or taken-over job continuing to spend AI tokens and queue for AI slots until its next DB write notices; with a 24 h worker slot wait it could otherwise block for hours.

items.name: Epoch
items.what: job.epoch is in the claim filter and the fence; next set/regenerate queue epoch+1 only while the stored epoch equals the one read. Also stamps generation.epoch, settled_epoch, AI call records, and is returned in RunActionStarted.
items.where: SHARED field (remediation uses it as version, mapper as generation). Scenario: crud/scenarios.py:499-531; runs.py:421-431; plan_progress.py:54,71,76; path_writing.py:189,258. API field schemas/scenarios.py:231
items.protects_against: A stale message of an earlier action (old next set) running against the new job; two concurrent next-set clicks both queuing. API-visible (epoch, generation_epoch): removal is class C.

items.name: Reaper: expired leases
items.what: Beat task every 60 s scans the 3 job collections for running jobs with lease_until in the past: requeues and re-sends them while attempts < 5, else fails them job_abandoned/worker_stopped. Also fails stale admin jobs.
items.protects_against: Worker pod killed or OOM mid-job (ack is at start, task_acks_late=False) leaves the run stuck in 'running' forever with no message to redeliver.

items.name: Reaper: re-send of lost messages
items.what: Finds jobs queued > 120 s; if the queue is empty (or after 900 s anyway) moves due_at and sends the message again; counts resends and fails the job never_started after 5. Reads each queue size once per pass.
items.protects_against: Broker down at send time, Redis flushed or restarted, or a retry message lost: the record says queued but no message exists, so the job would never start.

items.name: Reaper: job gauges for Grafana
items.what: Each pass aggregates queued/retrying/running/failed-24h jobs per task from all job collections into the tsg_jobs_current gauge, zeroing labels that ended; also stamps reaper last-start/last-pass times.
items.protects_against: Operator cannot see a backlog or a dead reaper on the dashboard. No functional safeguard for a run; purely observability.

items.name: Outage back-off and attempt limit
items.what: A TEMPORARY_ERROR (Unavailable, Mongo, Redis, SQL in progress) gives the job back queued with due_at = now + 15/30/60/120 s and task.retry(countdown); after Lease.MAX_ATTEMPTS=5 the job fails 'unavailable'. Claim refuses jobs not yet due (5 s skew).
items.protects_against: A short AI gateway or MongoDB outage failing every in-flight run for good; or a job retrying in a tight loop and burning tokens during a 429 storm.

items.name: Retry notice (job.retry)
items.what: Stores reason, message, attempt, max_attempts, retry_at on the record while a job waits out an outage or a refused send; shown as `retrying` on status, jobs list and admin monitor until the next claim clears it.
items.where: SHARED. crud/jobs.py:46-54,239-243; worker/jobs.py:185-186; celery_app.py:140-143; schemas/jobs.py:11-31; readers domain/jobs.py:235-282, domain/scenario/session.py:472
items.protects_against: User sees a run sitting in 'queued' for minutes with no explanation during an AI outage. API-visible field: removing it is class C (user loses why and when the next try comes).

items.name: Controls retry notice (controls_delivery.retry)
items.what: Second notice path for the controls stage: note_controls_outage writes the delivery's outage on the session; controls_retry_notice_of shows it only while controls_waiting > 0.
items.protects_against: Controls stuck 'being matched' during a rerank/embedding outage with no reason shown. Duplicates the job.retry notice because controls do not run as a leased job.

items.name: Controls message retry ladder
items.what: tsg_map_controls catches TEMPORARY_ERRORS itself: Celery retry with 15/30/60 s up to Controls.MAX_MESSAGE_RETRIES=3, then gives up and leaves it to the sweep (600 s).
items.protects_against: Search/rerank outage during control matching dropping the message so scenarios never get controls. Re-implements back-off outside run_leased_job.

items.name: Controls delivery lease (per run)
items.what: controls_delivery {task_id, until} on the session: only one tsg_map_controls delivery maps a run at a time; maps 6 scenarios per turn, then hands over to a fresh message; released when none wait; _taken_over stops a superseded delivery.
items.protects_against: Several map_controls messages (one is sent per saved scenario, write_job.py:115,135) all mapping the same run at once and exceeding the reranker cap; one run hogging a worker thread while others wait.

items.name: Per-scenario controls lease
items.what: Each scenario's controls.{status,task_id,lease_until,attempts} is claimed, renewed every 30 s and fenced like a job (max 5 attempts); outcome written only while the claim holds.
items.where: SCENARIO + REMEDIATION (plan job claims the same lease: remediation.py:169-217). crud/scenarios.py:78-87,164-174,271-345; controls_job.py:181-219,252-281
items.protects_against: Pod killed while mapping one scenario leaves its controls 'running' forever; two deliveries (run's and a plan's) saving different control lists for one scenario.

items.name: Controls sweep of stalled records
items.what: Beat task every 300 s: cancels controls waiting on a cancelled run, deletes scenarios of a deleted run, fails controls abandoned after 5 attempts, requeues queued>600 s / expired / failed>30 min ones, sends one message per run with no live delivery.
items.where: SCENARIO-ONLY. tasks.py:72-75; controls_job.py:75-100; work_control.py:210-243; crud/scenarios.py:347-377,618-623; beat celery_app.py:72
items.protects_against: Lost map_controls message or dead pod leaves scenarios showing 'controls being matched' forever; orphan scenarios written by a job racing a delete. It is a second reaper for the controls stage.

items.name: Cancel and resume
items.what: Cancel flips the run's job to cancelled (lease fence then fails -> LeaseLost stops the worker), cancels its queued/running controls, stamps who/when; a later next set/regenerate resumes cancelled controls with guards against a newer cancel or delete.
items.where: SCENARIO ~110: work_control.py:78-106,135-168; domain/jobs.py:61-66,97-109; worker/jobs.py:144-155. REMEDIATION ~40: work_control.py:108-133; domain/jobs.py:129-141
items.protects_against: User cannot stop a wrong or runaway run and it keeps spending AI tokens. Frozen API endpoints: removal is class C. resume_scenario_controls (34 lines) guards a cancel/delete racing a resume.

items.name: Delete with deleting mark
items.what: Delete marks the session, re-checks that no job, controls or plan is working (else 409 cancel_first naming plans), then deletes SQL operation records, scenarios, plans and the run; new actions refuse a marked run.
items.where: SCENARIO-ONLY. work_control.py:170-208; domain/jobs.py:68-82,112-126; crud/scenarios.py:572-575 and the DELETING_MARK filter at :508
items.protects_against: A job writing scenarios into a run while it is deleted (orphan cards), or a next set starting mid-delete. Frozen API: class C if removed.

items.name: Work list and admin job monitor
items.what: GET jobs: the caller's queued/running runs, plans and mappings (max 200 each) with progress and retry notice; admin monitor lists any job across collections plus queue length and online workers; admin job cancel.
items.protects_against: User or operator cannot see what is still running or why a queue is backed up. Frozen API endpoints: class C if removed.

items.name: Idempotency key and request hash
items.what: Start takes the caller's Idempotency-Key or derives one (sha256 of caller, method, path, body, 60 s window); a unique index plus request_hash replays the same run (200), 409s a different body, 409 duplicate_request for a derived repeat.
items.where: SHARED dep (scenario, remediation, mapper routes). api/deps.py:55-84; domain/shared/idempotency.py (17); scenario: runs.py:99-111,121-136; crud/scenarios.py:472-478,487-497; middleware.py:56-57
items.protects_against: Double click or client retry after a timeout starts two runs for one asset and pays for the AI twice. Response codes and header are frozen API: class C if changed.

items.name: Status publish (Redis) and SSE stream
items.what: After every saved change a worker publishes the record id on a Redis channel; one pattern subscription per API process fans out to SSE streams, which re-read status from MongoDB, coalesce 0.25 s, and re-read every 30 s anyway.
items.where: SHARED. realtime/publisher.py (42); realtime/event_hub.py (100); api/status_stream.py (51); routes scenarios.py:180-213, service_mapper.py:75-86; JOB_COLLECTIONS worker/jobs.py:50-54; ~15 publish calls
items.protects_against: UI would have to poll status; with only the 30 s re-read, progress would lag up to 30 s. The hub's reconnect/RESYNC covers a Redis drop silently ending all live updates. SSE endpoints are frozen API.

items.name: Per-stage timings
items.what: timings.threats_s, scenarios_s, controls_s kept for the latest action only: plan job time, $min writing_started_at, controls seconds $inc'd only for cards queued after the latest action began, reset on resume and new action.
items.where: SCENARIO-ONLY. tasks.py:83,107; write_job.py:110-112; plan_progress.py:116,127,138-144; crud/scenarios.py:441-442,566-569; controls_job.py:171,176-177; work_control.py:155-157; session.py:458-469
items.protects_against: Status showing stale or summed times from earlier actions (owner rule 2026-10-28). Shown in the API as StageTimings: removal is class C. Remediation keeps its own job.timings.

items.name: Progress records (plan paths and counts)
items.what: PlanProgress writes each path's state, plan figures and scenario counts in one fenced write and publishes; counts are recounted by aggregate after every controls change, guarded by counts_at so an older count never overwrites a newer.
items.where: SCENARIO-ONLY. worker/scenario/plan_progress.py (144); crud/scenarios.py:533-570; controls_job.py:91-100. The counts_at guard exists because job writes and controls deliveries recount concurrently
items.protects_against: Progress bar showing wrong numbers when the write job and parallel control mappings update counts at once; a path failure losing its spare replacement; counts written by a delivery that lost its lease.

items.name: Crash-safe re-delivery of the write job
items.what: A retried write job first serves paths whose scenario is already saved (no AI call), skips paths this epoch already settled, heals a regenerate whose new version was saved but not linked, and rescues given-up paths that did get written.
items.protects_against: Pod killed between saving a scenario and the fenced plan write: the retry would write and pay for the same scenarios again, or leave a path marked failed although its card exists.

items.name: AI outage handling in the scenario flow
items.what: Outages (Unavailable with AiOutage reason) retry the whole job; on the last attempt each path gets its own failure card with the outage wording; a path with outage is left for a later set (max path attempts); evidence-search outages hold a path back.
items.where: SCENARIO ~75: write_job.py:37-48,165-192; path_writing.py:59-65,199-206; plan_progress.py:67-72; tasks.py:86-87; controls_job.py:194-198. SHARED ~30: exceptions.py:105-111,160-163; shared/parallel.py:33-45
items.protects_against: One path's AI outage failing the whole run and discarding scenarios already written; a failure card that does not say it was an outage (regenerable) versus a real refusal.

items.name: AI answer reuse (same job and threat-finding across runs)
items.what: Before a chat call, looks up tsg_ai_call_texts for an ok answer to the same prompt hash by this record+epoch+task; for gate and gap-fill also any run's answer within CII_THREAT_FINDING_REUSE_HOURS (24).
items.where: Same-job part SHARED (4 callers in all 3 modules). Cross-run part SCENARIO-ONLY (~10 lines). ai/chat.py:92-101,215-236,308-309; crud/ai_calls.py:15,32-48; constants common.py:158-160, ai_limits.py:45-47
items.protects_against: A job retried after a crash or outage paying again for answers it already got; a second Start on the same asset within 24 h re-asking the identical threat-finding question (tokens and about a minute).

items.name: Stage hand-over and message priority
items.what: hand_over ends a stage and queues the next task on the same record and epoch in one fenced write, sent at priority 0; retries and reaper re-sends also go at 0, new work at 3, a busy entity's plans at 6.
items.where: hand_over SCENARIO-ONLY callers (tasks.py:110, plan_progress.py:98) but lives in worker/jobs.py:61-66. Priorities SHARED: celery_app.py:60-61; constants jobs.py:83-86; priority 6 only at remediation/plans.py:313
items.protects_against: A run that already found threats waiting behind every newly started run before writing (10 users at once: started runs finish before new ones begin). Without it, time to first scenario grows under load.

items.name: Hand-back on worker shutdown
items.what: On SIGTERM, after 90 s a thread gives every still-held lease back: job requeued now with its attempt returned and re-sent at priority 0; a scenario's controls requeued and the delivery lease freed. Logs it as handed back, not lost.
items.where: SHARED ~40: lease_renewal.py:18-21,39-40,63-76; worker/jobs.py:135-141,151-152; lifecycle.py:208-212. SCENARIO ~15: controls_job.py:272-281; attempt_returned in crud/scenarios.py:321,326
items.protects_against: A deploy or pod eviction mid-job: without it the job waits up to 120 s lease + 60 s reaper before restarting and each rollout burns one of its 5 attempts.

items.name: Waiting for another job
items.what: WaitingForAnotherJob gives the job back without using an attempt, polls every 15 s, flags job.waiting, and fails job_abandoned after 3,600 s; counted as outcome 'waiting' in metrics.
items.where: SHARED infrastructure with NO scenario user: raised only at worker/remediation.py:177,199,205. worker/jobs.py:57-58,109-111,118-119,199-217; crud/jobs.py:107; lifecycle.py:188
items.protects_against: A remediation plan job starting while the run's controls delivery is still mapping that scenario's controls: it waits instead of failing or mapping twice. Not a scenario decision.

items.name: Worker lifecycle: heartbeat, job clock, send
items.what: Start-up checks and index creation, a Redis heartbeat per queue every 20 s plus a liveness file, per-task start/finish log and duration/outcome metrics, request-id header on messages, send_job that reports a refused send.
items.protects_against: /ready passing with no worker consuming a queue (jobs accepted but never run); a hung worker not restarted by the liveness probe; logs that cannot tie a job to the API request that started it.

tests.report:
Scope: read-only scan (wc, grep, AST count over tests/**/*.py). No file changed, nothing run.

(b) API-LEVEL vs INTERNALS
- 72 test files reference app/domain/scenario, app/worker/scenario or app/crud/scenarios: 95 distinct names, 636 references (24 names start with "_"). By module: write.py 26 names, session.py 22, plan.py 15, crud/scenarios 11, worker tasks 6, controls_job 4, path_writing 4, write_job 3, runs 3, plan_progress 1. Not counted: methods called on instances (ThreatScenarioService, repositories, PathWriter) and constructor keyword names.
- Survive a rewrite untouched (HTTP + stored records only), about 3,900 lines: test_runs, test_review, test_run_actions, test_job_control, test_d51_idempotency, test_d51_cancel_controls, test_accept_v1_body, test_outage_paths_rewritten, test_promotion, test_d51_plans, test_outside_contract, external_intelligence/test_end_to_end. They hold ONLY IF a narrow seam keeps its names: tests/service_builders.threat_scenario_service (10 files; builds ThreatScenarioService with 11 keyword dependencies), get_threat_scenario_repository (12 files), get_threat_scenario_session_repository (13 files), get_threat_scenario_service (7 files), get_scenario_write_job / get_controls_job / send_job / publish_session_status as module attributes (monkeypatched 11 times), tasks.find_threats / map_controls / PLAN_JOB_FIELDS.
- Must be edited by any rename or signature change, about 9,000 lines: test_scenario_writing (48 refs, 17 names), test_control_mapping (46/9), test_scenario_goldens_session (39/5), evidence_story (36/15), test_attack_paths, test_threat_finding, test_scenario_sets, test_run_board, test_controls_fixes, test_property_selection, test_lean_gate and about 30 small rule files.
- Removing a class costs: ThreatScenarioService 21 refs/5 files + service_builders; ControlMapper 21/5; the two repository classes 37 refs/9+8 files; RunControls 8/3; PathWriter 4/2; PlanProgress 1; 38 direct constructor calls of worker/domain classes in tests.
- 33 monkeypatch.setattr calls target scenario module attributes (write.get_settings x4, write_job.send_job x3, write_job.get_scenario_write_job x3, controls_job.get_controls_job x3, controls_job.publish_session_status x3, runs.utc_now / uuid / session_status_from_record / check_session_ready_for_review / build_run_context): those names must stay importable at module level in the same module.
Top 30 names (references, files): write.build_scenario_id 53/5; session.build_status_board 31/9; session.build_scenario_view 26/8; plan.build_plan 24/8; write.write_scenario_set 22/7; crud.get_threat_scenario_repository 21/12; runs.ThreatScenarioService 21/5; write.ControlMapper 21/5; crud.ThreatScenarioSessionRepository 21/9; crud.get_threat_scenario_session_repository 20/13; runs.get_threat_scenario_service 20/7; crud.ThreatScenarioRepository 16/8; write.build_writer_prompt 15/4; write.find_duplicate_scenario_id 15/2; write.build_writer_input 14/5; write.build_scenario_card 14/6; write_job.find_evidence_outage 12/4; write.build_writer_system_prompt 12/5; plan.describe_asset_for_ai 12/5; session.pick_replacement_path 12/2; write.build_control_query 10/5; write._apply_safety_checks 9/5; write.pick_controls_to_keep 9/1; tasks.map_controls 8/4; write.WRITER_SYSTEM_PROMPT 8/3; tasks.PLAN_JOB_FIELDS 8/3; controls_job.RunControls 8/3; crud.DELETING_MARK 7/2; plan._merge_duplicate_threats 7/2; tasks.find_threats 6/3.

(c) WHAT THE GOLDENS PIN (4 test files, 1,117 lines; helper tests/scenario_goldens.py 155; 22 JSON files in tests/goldens/scenario, 20 compared + 2 inputs)
- None goes through HTTP: all four call internals directly, so they pin function names and signatures as well as output. Comparison is parsed-JSON equality (key order and whitespace free; datetimes become "<datetime>"; dataclasses/models/enums flattened), regenerated with CII_WRITE_GOLDENS=1.
- Plan (7 tests, plan_*.json): find_threats(chat, search, rerank, embeddings) bound by partial, build_plan, build_plan_trace. Pins every system+user prompt per AI ask IN ORDER (so call count and call order), every embedding text and reranker (query, documents) call in order, the stored plan and trace, and the refusal payloads. Assumes THREATS_PER_QUESTION=40 and AI_BATCHES_AT_ONCE=1.
- Write (2 tests, write_original/write_evidence): PathWriter(run, chat, live, style).write_scenario_set(slots, last_try, epoch) yielding (path_id, outcome), writer.threats, build_scenario_card, build_failure_card. Pins every writer prompt in order (write then rewrite), every stored card (scenario ids, blocked, failed, evidence story, version 2) and the duplicate findings.
- Controls (4 tests, controls_*.json): ControlMapper, build_controls_record, RunControls. Pins each card's control query, reranker calls, stored controls record, reuse vs search-again, and that all queries go in ONE embedding call.
- Session (7 tests, session_*.json): ThreatScenarioService(11 keyword parts as MagicMock), session.* functions, build_status_board, build_scenario_view. Pins start-check errors and frozen context, replay fingerprint, 12 status boards and 11 scenario views (the API JSON the UI reads), review/accept/cancel rules, next-set progress rules, library lookups.
- Consequence: a class A/B change that merges two AI calls, reorders calls, or changes a stored field breaks a golden; a pure rename only needs the test file's imports and call lines edited, never the JSON.

(d) tests/test_code_conventions.py (353 lines) RULES THAT BIND THE REWRITE
- Function cap 40 lines everywhere, scenario included. Today plan.py has 5 functions of 35-37 lines and write.py 2: folding one-use helpers inline will hit the cap quickly.
- File cap 500, lifted only for app/domain/scenario/, app/crud/scenarios.py, app/schemas/scenario_internal.py, app/schemas/scenarios.py. NOT lifted for app/worker/scenario/ (5 files, 1,005 lines): merging them into one file fails unless the result is under 500 or it moves into domain/scenario.
- Class cap 7 public methods / 150 lines; exempt files include domain/scenario/runs.py and crud/scenarios.py, not write.py or worker/scenario. Replacing classes with plain functions removes this limit.
- Layers: domain may import core, schemas, crud, ai, search, realtime, worker; worker may import domain; api may not import worker; crud only core/schemas. domain/shared may not import domain.scenario.
- Database calls (find, update_one, aggregate...) only in app/crud. Pydantic models only in schemas/ or domain/.
- No functools.lru_cache/cache (use @singleton). Log event names from the LogEvent enum; fixed log field names. Inline raise messages allowed only in crud, domain, schemas (worker code must use ErrorMessage). No datetime.now()/time.time() (app.core.clock).
- ruff check + ruff format must pass (line length 120; E, F, I, B, UP, S, SIM). No naming-convention test exists; every module must sit in a layer folder.
